claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has good plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength.
As-cast equimolar CoCrFeNiTi is a homogeneous, single-phase simple solid solution.
The homogeneous CoCrFeNiTi solid solution lacks nanoscale obstacles such as short-range chemical order or finely dispersed precipitates.
Nanoscale chemical ordering and fine precipitates can impede or pin dislocations.
The absence of nanoscale obstacles permits relatively unobstructed dislocation glide and dynamic recovery in as-cast CoCrFeNiTi.
Ready dislocation glide and dynamic recovery favor ductility while limiting work hardening.
A controlled mild aging or annealing treatment can induce nanoscale chemical ordering or clustering in CoCrFeNiTi without producing coarse precipitates.
Induced nanoscale order or fine clusters will create short-range barriers to dislocation motion.
Greater dislocation pinning from nanoscale order will increase hardness and yield or compressive strength.
Greater dislocation pinning from nanoscale order will reduce homogeneous plastic strain.
The aged alloy should display more dislocation pile-up or lower dislocation mobility than the as-cast alloy.
The comparison should hold composition constant by testing as-cast and aged equimolar CoCrFeNiTi samples.
The proposed hypothesis is limited to ambient temperature through 600 °C and moderate strain rates around 1×10^-3 s^-1 under uniaxial tension or compression.
The hypothesis may not apply if aging produces coarse brittle precipitates.
Failure of aging to produce a statistically significant hardness and strength increase, or failure to reveal increased dislocation pinning, would falsify the proposed explanation.
